- ChildModeGuard — lib/core/navigation/guards/child_mode_guard.dart:38 try / :50 catch -> child_mode_guard_failed_closed, `if (!resolver.isResolved) resolver.next(false);` (:56). Fail-CLOSED. Wired on child-only routes (app_router.dart:202,208,214,...).

No source change needed — fix is complete and matches the spec exactly.
- Code: `/home/daniel/repos/learning-tracker/learning_tracker/lib/app/router/guards/auth_guard.dart:42-85`, `/home/daniel/repos/learning-tracker/learning_tracker/lib/core/navigation/guards/restore_guard.dart:49-95`, `/home/daniel/repos/learning-tracker/learning_tracker/lib/core/navigation/guards/profile_guard.dart:44-54`, `/home/daniel/repos/learning-tracker/learning_tracker/lib/core/navigation/guards/pin_guard.dart:89-126`, `/home/daniel/repos/learning-tracker/learning_tracker/lib/core/navigation/guards/child_mode_guard.dart:38-58`, `/home/daniel/repos/learning-tracker/learning_tracker/lib/app/router/app_router.dart:61-127`, `/home/daniel/repos/learning-tracker/learning_tracker/lib/app/router/router_provider.dart:36-80`, `/home/daniel/repos/learning-tracker/learning_tracker/test/core/navigation/auth_guard_test.dart:362`, `/home/daniel/repos/learning-tracker/learning_tracker/test/core/navigation/restore_guard_test.dart:361`, `/home/daniel/repos/learning-tracker/learning_tracker/test/core/navigation/profile_guard_test.dart:199`, `/home/daniel/repos/learning-tracker/learning_tracker/test/core/navigation/pin_guard_test.dart:613`, `/home/daniel/repos/learning-tracker/learning_tracker/test/core/navigation/child_mode_guard_test.dart:213`
- Confirm on-device: This is a defensive fail-safe; you cannot trigger a guard throw with normal taps. To exercise the no-lockout behavior on-device (1080x2340), you must corrupt the state each guard reads so its body throws, then confirm the app still navigates (never freezes on a blank/black screen with no progress).

PREP (per session):
- adb connect 100.72.6.10:PORT ; adb -s <serial> shell to get a shell.
- App package: find with `adb shell pm list packages | grep -i tracker` (e.g. ai.orvex.learning_tracker / com.example.learning_tracker). Use $PKG below.
- To watch which guard fired: `adb logcat | grep -E "auth_guard_failed_safe_to_signin|restore_guard_failed_safe_allow|profile_guard_failed_safe_allow|pin_guard_failed_closed|child_mode_guard_failed_closed"` (AppLogger/Talker tags). Seeing one of these log lines + the app moving = fix working.

(A) AuthGuard fail-SAFE -> SignIn (corrupt device_registry):
1. Cold start once and complete intro so `intro_seen=true` but stay signed out (onboarding incomplete) so AuthGuard hits the registry-read branch.
2. Force-stop: `adb shell am force-stop $PKG`.
3. Corrupt the registry DB so driftDatabase open/getAllAccounts throws: `adb shell run-as $PKG sh -c 'find /data/data/$PKG -name "device_registry*"'` then overwrite it: `adb shell run-as $PKG sh -c 'echo notasqlite > <path>/device_registry.sqlite'` (truncate the -wal/-shm too). If run-as is blocked (release build), instead clear app data (`adb shell pm clear $PKG`) to force the no-accounts path — that alone won't throw, so for the throw path use a debug build where run-as works.
4. Launch: `adb shell monkey -p $PKG 1` (or tap the launcher icon ~center-bottom of home screen).
5. EXPECT: app lands on the Sign-In screen (not a hang). Logcat shows auth_guard_failed_safe_to_signin.

(B) ChildModeGuard fail-CLOSED (corrupt profile mode):
1. Sign in, create/select a profile, reach the AppShell.
2. Force-stop, then corrupt the active profile's `mode` column to a value that is neither 'adult' nor 'child' (ProfileMode.fromStorageKey throws ArgumentError): `adb shell run-as $PKG sqlite3 <path>/user_*.sqlite "UPDATE profiles SET mode='garbage' WHERE id=<selectedId>;"`.
3. Re-launch and tap into a child-only route (a learning/tracking surface guarded by childModeGuard, e.g. the learn tab item top-center, then a track tile).
4. EXPECT: navigation is BLOCKED — you stay on the current screen / get bounced back, NOT a frozen black screen. Logcat shows child_mode_guard_failed_closed.

(C) PinGuard fail-CLOSED (secure-storage / lockout throw):
1. Sign in as an adult and trigger a PIN-gated route: tap the persistent profile-switcher role label at the very TOP of the shell (~x540,y90), choose Parent/Adult mode, or open Settings (bottom tab, far right ~x980,y2270) -> a PIN-protected parent action. This pushes the parent-PIN dialog.
2. To force a throw without storage tampering: enter a WRONG PIN repeatedly past the lockout threshold so PinLockoutException is thrown from promptForPin/verify. Tap keypad digits in the dialog (keypad occupies the lower-center; 4-digit entry) and submit wrong codes ~6+ times.
3. EXPECT: the navigation is denied — the gated screen does NOT open and you remain on the prior screen (you can retry/cancel), NOT a permanent hang. Logcat shows pin_guard_failed_closed.

(D) Restore/Profile fail-OPEN are harder to force on device (need the user DB read to throw mid-navigation); the AuthGuard repro (A) is the clearest functional demonstration of the no-lockout invariant. For Profile/Restore, the meaningful on-device check is the negative: with a corrupt user DB the app must still reach the AppShell/Settings (fail-open) rather than freeze — watch for profile_guard_failed_safe_allow / restore_guard_failed_safe_allow in logcat with the app still advancing.

PASS CRITERIA (all guards): the app NEVER sits on a blank/non-interactive screen after a guarded navigation; it either advances (auth/restore/profile) or cleanly stays/bounces back (pin/child) and a *_failed_* log line is emitted. A hang (spinner forever / black screen, no log) = regression.
- Expected: Post-fix: no guarded navigation can hang. On any unexpected throw inside onNavigation each guard catches it, logs a *_failed_safe/_closed event, and resolves the NavigationResolver exactly once (guarded by `if (!resolver.isResolved)` so it never double-resolves a partially-resolved redirect): AuthGuard routes to SignInRoute and next(false); RestoreGuard and ProfileGuard fail-open with next() (navigation proceeds to the device-restore-optional shell / Settings); PinGuard and ChildModeGuard fail-closed with next(false) (the gated/child-only route is blocked, user stays put and can retry). The AutoRoute completer is always completed, so the UI never freezes on a blank screen.
- Risk: 1. Double-resolve guard: every catch block first checks `if (!resolver.isResolved)`. This matters because the happy path may have already called resolver.next()/next(false) and only the *subsequent* router.replace / DB close threw — re-resolving would throw a 'resolver already completed' assert. Tester should confirm no second resolve in that ordering (e.g. AuthGuard where registry.close() in finally could throw after resolver.next(false)).
2. Security posture per guard must NOT be inverted: PinGuard and ChildModeGuard MUST fail CLOSED (next(false)). A regression that flips these to next() would silently grant access to PIN-gated / child-only routes on a transient storage error — verify repro (B)/(C) BLOCK, not allow.
3. AuthGuard catch issues router.replace(SignInRoute) even when the body already redirected to AppIntro/AccountPicker before throwing; because of the isResolved check it only fires if nothing resolved yet, so a throw mid-redirect could leave the in-flight replace + a next(false) — tester should confirm the landing screen is sane (SignIn) and not a flicker between two routes.
4. RestoreGuard/ProfileGuard fail-open means a genuinely-needed restore/profile-pick could be skipped on a transient DB error; the user can still restore from Settings and the shell self-corrects the no-profile state, but tester should note if a fail-open masks a real corrupt-DB condition (app proceeds with empty data).
5. These throws are not reachable via normal UI; on-device verification requires debug build + run-as/sqlite3 tampering or the PIN-lockout path. On a release build without run-as, only (C) the PIN-lockout repro is achievable; (A)/(B)/(D) need a debuggable build.
6. PinLockoutException is the realistic real-world trigger for PinGuard's catch — confirm that after lockout the user is held on the current screen and can still navigate elsewhere (back button works), i.e. the lockout doesn't strand the whole app.

PART 1 — "Discard local" account-merge no longer crashes.
- Root cause that was fixed: the discard-local path used to do update().replace() on a partial (id + passwordHash-only) row, which throws Drift InvalidDataException ("requires a complete row") and crashed the collision-resolution flow.

=== FLOW A — Discard-local merge no longer crashes (the headline fix) ===
PRECONDITION / state to set:
1. You need a LOCAL-born account on the device whose email ALSO already exists as a verified CLOUD (Firebase) account. Easiest setup: (a) on a throwaway install, sign up a cloud account with email X + password P_cloud and verify it via the inbox link; (b) reinstall / wipe app data; (c) create a LOCAL-only account using the SAME email X with a DIFFERENT password P_local (skip cloud during onboarding so the account is local-born), and add a profile + a little local progress (mark one task) so there is "purely-local" data to discard.
NAVIGATE:
2. From the app shell, open Settings (gear). Scroll to the "Backup & Sync" card (blue card). Because the account is local-born it shows the "LOCAL ONLY — Upgrade to sync" CTA. Tap "Upgrade to Cloud" (button at upgrade_to_cloud_screen entry; backup_sync_section.dart:168/245). Screen 1080x2340: the button is the peach/orange filled button near the bottom of the card.
3. On the "Back up your account" screen, type P_local in "Confirm your password" and tap "Upgrade to Cloud".
4. Because the email already exists in Firebase, the EmailCollisionException fires and the red "A cloud account already exists with this email" block appears (the _CollisionBlock).
5. Tap the SECOND option tile: "Keep cloud, discard local".
6. In "Cloud account password" type P_cloud (the EXISTING cloud account's password).
7. TICK the acknowledgement checkbox ("I understand that cloud data will replace any purely-local changes on this device.").
8. Tap "Discard local and sign in".
EXPECTED (post-fix): the operation completes — spinner, then the green "You're backed up!" success block (_PhaseSuccess). The app must NOT crash / show a red error screen / drop to a Drift InvalidDataException. After success the local password hash is cleared and the profile is flipped to cloud-born; subsequent pull brings down cloud data.
PRE-FIX behavior (to recognise a regression): immediately after tapping "Discard local and sign in" the flow throws InvalidDataException and surfaces as a "Merge failed: ..." error (or a hard crash), never reaching the success block.
NEGATIVE CHECKS while here: (a) tap "Discard local and sign in" WITHOUT ticking the checkbox → expect inline error "Please acknowledge that local data will be replaced..." and NO execution; (b) leave cloud password blank → "Please enter your cloud account password."; (c) wrong cloud password → "Incorrect cloud account password." and you stay on the collision block (no crash).

=== FLOW B — Sign-in connectivity routing online vs offline ===
B1 (online, cloud account): with Wi-Fi/data ON, on the Sign-In screen enter a registered cloud email + correct password, Sign In → expect normal Firebase sign-in and navigation into the app (picker or shell).
B2 (OFFLINE cloud restore — the key offline branch): put the phone in Airplane mode (adb: `adb -s 100.72.6.10:PORT shell cmd connectivity airplane-mode enable`, or toggle in quick settings). On the same device where that cloud account previously signed in (local Drift data present), enter the cloud email + password and Sign In. EXPECTED: sign-in still succeeds OFFLINE — _tryOfflineCloudRestore swaps to the local DB and lands you in the app shell, no spinner-hang, no "network-request-failed". 
B3 (offline, no local data for that account): still in Airplane mode, sign in with a cloud email that has NEVER signed in on this device. EXPECTED: clean error message (authLocalDataMissing — e.g. "local data missing / can't sign in offline"), NOT an indefinite spinner or crash. The 15s watchdog (sign_in_controller.dart:571) must also resolve any hang into a timeout error.
B4 (offline, totally unknown email): Airplane mode, enter a random unregistered email + password. EXPECTED: authEmailOfflineUnreachable message ("needs internet"), no crash.
Re-enable connectivity afterward: `adb shell cmd connectivity airplane-mode disable`.
- Expected: Discard-local merge: tapping "Discard local and sign in" (with acknowledgement ticked + correct cloud password) completes to the green "You're backed up!" success block; the profile flips to cloud-born and the local password hash is cleared via a TARGETED partial UPDATE (clearPasswordHash) — no Drift InvalidDataException, no crash. Sign-in routing: ONLINE registered cloud accounts go through Firebase; OFFLINE a previously-signed-in cloud account is restored from local Drift and reaches the app shell; OFFLINE with no local data shows authLocalDataMissing; OFFLINE unknown email shows authEmailOfflineUnreachable. All branches gate on internetConnectionCheckerProvider.hasConnection rather than throwing raw network exceptions.
- Risk: EDGE/RISK NOTES FOR TESTER:
1. Entry-point gating: the "Upgrade to Cloud" CTA (and thus the whole collision/discard flow) is ONLY rendered when the active session is LOCAL-born (backup_sync_section.dart:38-43, isLocalAuth). A cloud-born or 'Connecting…' state hides it (:30-36). If you can't find the button, you're signed in as cloud-born — the discard flow is unreachable by design.
2. Setup is the hard part: you genuinely need a verified Firebase cloud account AND a separate local-born account on the SAME email/different password to trigger EmailCollisionException. If the cloud account is UNVERIFIED, you'll hit the verification panel (_PhaseVerifying) instead of the collision block — that's a different branch, not the bug.
3. discardLocalCredentials only clears passwordHash; the actual local-vs-cloud data replacement happens on the subsequent SyncEngine pull (_pushLocalDataAfterUpgrade at upgrade_to_cloud_screen.dart:102-113 then pullOnLaunch). So immediately after "You're backed up!" the on-screen data may still show local rows until the pull lands — watch the sync status card settle. Verify cloud data actually wins after sync completes.
4. Offline detection depends on the internet_connection_checker package's host probe; on some networks a captive portal or DNS that resolves-but-can't-route may make hasConnection return true while Firebase still fails — in that case you'd fall into the online branch and see a Firebase network error rather than the offline message. True Airplane mode is the clean repro.
5. _requireInternet() in the upgrade screen only resets to _PhaseForm (clears the collision selection) when offline — so if you go offline mid-merge, you'll be bounced back to the password form with the "Internet connection is required to upgrade to cloud" message; re-entering the collision flow requires re-submitting.
6. The 15s sign-in watchdog (sign_in_controller.dart:571) and 10s Firebase timeouts (:663,:699) mean a flaky network shows a timeout error, not a permanent hang — don't mistake a slow-network timeout for the bug.
7. clearPasswordHash leaves the profile row otherwise intact then upgradeLocalToCloud overwrites tier/uid/updatedAt in a transaction (user_profile_dao.dart:106-119); if you inspect the DB between the two writes you'd briefly see a cloud-tier-ish row with null hash — that's expected, the two calls are sequential within executeKeepCloudDiscardLocal (not one transaction), so a crash BETWEEN them (e.g. kill app) could leave a passwordHash-null local-tier row. Low risk but worth noting for an interrupt test.
8. rg display artifact: a piped ripgrep in this environment rendered matched tokens as 'ln' (e.g. 'discardLocalCredentials' showed as 'lnLocalCredentials'); the real identifiers were confirmed via direct file reads and are correct in source. No action needed — just don't grep-verify with that exact pipeline.

### ✅ present — PRESENT (true). The "I am in Israel" manual toggle now STICKS and is not reverted by a background reload. Two layers implement this:

1) Primary fix — race guard in InIsraelNotifier (lib/features/sacred_time/presentation/providers/sacred_location_provider.dart:123-155). The notifier carries a per-instance bool `_explicitlySet` (declared :130). `build()` returns false and kicks off async `_load()` (:132-136). `_load()` (:138-146) bails early if `!ref.mounted || _explicitlySet` (:143) so a late-resuming prefs read cannot clobber a value the user just set. `setInIsrael(bool)` (:148-154) sets `_explicitlySet = true` FIRST, then `state = value`, then persists to SharedPreferences and pushes the sync snapshot. This kills the reload race: previously, flipping a location (setManualCity/detect at :55,:93) calls `ref.invalidate(inIsraelProvider)`, which rebuilds the notifier and re-triggers the async `_load()`; that `_load()` could resume AFTER `setInIsrael` and overwrite the user's choice with the stale country-derived default. The guard makes an explicit set win.

2) Supporting fix — sync no longer clobbers it. UiPreferencesMerger (lib/core/sync/merge/ui_preferences_merger.dart:135-140) deliberately IGNORES any sacred_time block in pulled Firestore docs (DEC-26/WS6); sacred-time/location/in-Israel is device-scoped in SharedPreferences via SacredTimePreferences (lib/features/sacred_time/data/services/sacred_time_preferences.dart:59-65, keys `sacred_time_in_israel`). So a background pull / second-profile sync round-trip cannot overwrite the device-global toggle.

Persistence key `sacred_time_in_israel` is read at sacred_time_preferences.dart:59 and written at :63. Introduced in commit 952252d9 'fix(sacred_time): inIsrael reload race + coverage wave 9'.
- Code: `/home/daniel/repos/learning-tracker/learning_tracker/lib/features/sacred_time/presentation/providers/sacred_location_provider.dart:123-155 (InIsraelNotifier; _explicitlySet declared :130, guard :143, setInIsrael :148-154)`, `/home/daniel/repos/learning-tracker/learning_tracker/lib/features/sacred_time/presentation/providers/sacred_location_provider.dart:55,93 (ref.invalidate(inIsraelProvider) on detect/setManualCity — the rebuild that re-triggers _load)`, `/home/daniel/repos/learning-tracker/learning_tracker/lib/features/sacred_time/data/services/sacred_time_preferences.dart:59-65 (readInIsrael/writeInIsrael, key sacred_time_in_israel)`, `/home/daniel/repos/learning-tracker/learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/merge/ui_preferences_merger.dart:135-140 (DEC-26: sacred_time block ignored on pull — device-scoped, no LWW clobber)`, `/home/daniel/repos/learning-tracker/learning_tracker/lib/features/sacred_time/presentation/widgets/sacred_time_settings_card.dart:228-268 (_InIsraelRow; Switch onChanged → setInIsrael, :261-264)`, `/home/daniel/repos/learning-tracker/learning_tracker/lib/features/settings/presentation/screens/settings_screen.dart:104 (card mounted in Settings)`, `/home/daniel/repos/learning-tracker/learning_tracker/test/features/sacred_time/sacred_location_and_data_test.dart:1113-1164 (active, non-skipped regression tests incl. ### ✅ present — Redemption Fulfil/Decline is single-tap guarded. The buttons live in `_RedemptionCard`, which was converted to a StatefulWidget (`_RedemptionCardState`) carrying a `bool _busy` flag and a `_run(action)` helper. `_run` returns early if `_busy` (so a second tap is dropped), sets `_busy=true` before awaiting the action, and clears it in a `finally` (guarded by `mounted`). Both buttons pass `onPressed: _busy ? null : () => _run(...)`, so during an in-flight fulfil/decline both buttons are disabled, preventing a double-fire AND a fulfil-then-decline race on the same card. ### ✅ present — CONFIRMED PRESENT. The crash guard lives in MagicLinkService._extractActionUri at /home/daniel/repos/learning-tracker/learning_tracker/lib/features/account/data/services/magic_link_service.dart:145-154. Before unwrapping a wrapped deep link (link= / deep_link_id= / continueUrl=), Uri.decodeComponent(next) is now wrapped in try/catch:

  final String decoded;
  try {
    decoded = Uri.decodeComponent(next);
  } on ArgumentError {
    return current;   // stop unwrapping, process the URI as-is
  }

Previously this was a bare `final decoded = Uri.decodeComponent(next);` (see git diff in commit 26564a6d). A malformed percent-encoding (e.g. "%%%") threw ArgumentError: Invalid URL encoding, which escaped the app_links stream listener (_appLinks.uriLinkStream.listen at line 86) uncaught and crashed/killed the deep-link service.

Wiring chain confirming this is the live path:
- App boots the listener once via magicLinkInitializationProvider (lib/features/account/presentation/providers/magic_link_providers.dart:30-32), watched in LearningTrackerApp.build (lib/app/learning_tracker_app.dart:39).
- MagicLinkService.initialize() processes both cold-start (getInitialLink, line 74) and warm (uriLinkStream, line 86) links; both route into _handleIncomingLink -> _extractActionUri.
- AndroidManifest registers exactly one autoVerify https deep-link host, torah-study-tracker.firebaseapp.com (android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:42-50), so EVERY real incoming external link flows through MagicLinkService — the patched code.

Regression guard: un-skipped test "malformed link= value (not a valid URI) falls through gracefully" at test/features/account/data/services/magic_link_service_test.dart:716-739 emits Uri.https with link=%%%not-a-uri and asserts the service still reaches isSignInWithEmailLink (no throw). Bug log: docs/planning/test-fix-bug-log.md:146-150.

- Expected: Tapping/firing a malformed deep link (invalid percent-encoding in a link=/deep_link_id= wrapper) must NOT crash the app or kill the deep-link listener. The service logs the incoming link, attempts to unwrap, hits the undecodable wrapper, stops unwrapping, and processes the original URI as-is. Because that original URI is not a recognized Firebase sign-in/verifyEmail link, it is silently ignored (isSignInWithEmailLink returns false -> early return) and the user stays where they are. No FATAL exception, no app restart, and subsequent legitimate magic links still process.
- Risk: see above

### F3 Offline → reconnect sync round-trip. (1) Go offline. The connectivity signal is a DNS/host probe stream `connectivityStreamProvider` (connectivity_providers.dart:27) seeded by `checker.hasConnection` then `onStatusChange`. app_shell.dart:111-116 watches it: `offlineBannerVisible = isCloudBorn && !isOnline` — local-born users NEVER see the banner (offline_top_banner.dart:3-5). (2) While offline, mark completions on the Learn/reader surface and create a track. Each completion goes through the single authoritative path CompletionWriter.commit/commitBatch (completion_writer.dart:546/82) which, in ONE Drift transaction, inserts both a `completion_events` row (canonical FR5 log) AND an `outbox` row (push queue). Track-create writes go through SyncWriteFacade (`_syncFacade?.pushBookmark/pushProfileProgram/pushStudyDayConfig`, track_creation_service.dart:325-374) which also enqueue outbox rows. Nothing is network-gated — all writes hit Drift first and queue. (3) Drift-first reads still render: the dashboard/progress/learn read from `completions_view` and DAOs, never from network, so marked items show ticked immediately while offline. The OfflineTopBanner (32px, `secondaryContainer`, `cloud_off` icon, string "Offline — changes will sync when you're back", semantics liveRegion offline_top_banner.dart:26-40) shows at top; its height is summed into the appBar PreferredSize at app_shell.dart:142-149. Sync surface in Settings (BackupSyncSection) shows offline + "N pending changes" (backup_sync_section.dart:59-65) and SyncStatusIndicator (if mounted) shows grey cloud_off "N queued" (sync_status_indicator.dart:44-49). (4) Reconnect. `_onConnectivityChange` (sync_orchestrator.dart:514) fires on the offline→online transition (requires previous==false, ignores the seeded first emission), recomputes status, then after a 1.5s debounce calls `_doFirestoreNetworkReset()` and `_drainOutbox('connectivity')` (sync_orchestrator.dart:537-555). A periodic 60s timer is a safety net but is gated on `_lastConnectivity==true` (sync_orchestrator.dart:506-509). (5) Drain: OutboxProcessor.drain (outbox_processor.dart:175) is single-flight (with a stale-guard reclaim), batches completions via pushCompletionsBatch and drains non-completion kinds one at a time with capped+jittered exponential backoff and dead-letters at 10 attempts. Committed rows are deleted; failed rows are markAttempted and retried. (6) SyncStatusIndicator/BackupSync transitions: `_recomputeOutboxStatus` (sync_orchestrator.dart:914) runs after every drain and on every connectivity change → offline→pending→synced (depth-driven), or degraded if rows are stuck. (7) Inbound merge of remote rows: completions use append-only insertIfAbsent with tombstone-resurrection (drift_merge_store.dart:211-263); LWW kinds (track_config, profile, bookmark, stage, learning_order) gate on remoteIsNewer with the ±5s clock-skew window falling back to Firestore synced_at (drift_merge_store.dart:111-146); bookmark/track ordering FK-guard skips a bookmark whose track has not yet synced (drift_merge_store.dart:412-418). No data loss; nothing is network-gated.
- Screens: App shell (top OfflineTopBanner + appBar PreferredSize sizing) — lib/app/router/app_shell.dart → Learn / reader completion-marking surface (writes via CompletionWriter → outbox) → Dashboard + Progress (Drift-first reads, must still render ticked items offline) → Track creation / program enrolment wizard (SyncWriteFacade queued writes) — lib/features/tracks/setup/domain/services/track_creation_service.dart → Settings → Backup & Sync section (offline/pending/syncing/synced/degraded states) — lib/features/settings/presentation/widgets/backup_sync_section.dart → SyncStatusIndicator widget (status icon/label — note: not currently mounted in any screen) — lib/features/sync/presentation/widgets/sync_status_indicator.dart
  - OfflineTopBanner visibility is gated on BOTH cloud-born AND offline: `offlineBannerVisible = isCloudBorn && !isOnline` (app_shell.dart:116). Verify a local-born user NEVER sees it (offline_top_banner.dart:3-5) and that the 32px banner height is actually added to the appBar PreferredSize (app_shell.dart:142,147-149) — if not summed, content overflows behind the status bar or leaves a gap.
  - Banner + indicator strings are HARD-CODED English, not localized: "Offline — changes will sync when you're back" (offline_top_banner.dart:38), "Connecting…"/"Offline" (backup_sync_section.dart:34,64), and all SyncStatusIndicator labels "Synced/Syncing/N pending/N queued/Sync error" (sync_status_indicator.dart:26-63). In a Hebrew UI these will not translate — flag as a localization gap.
  - SyncStatusIndicator is defined but rendered in NO screen (`SyncStatusIndicator(` has zero call sites in lib). The only live sync surface a tester can observe is Settings → Backup & Sync (backup_sync_section.dart:24 watches syncStatusProvider). Do not expect a top-bar sync chip; verify state transitions only in the Backup & Sync card.
  - Marking-while-offline must hit Drift first and stay rendered: CompletionWriter.commit writes completion_events + outbox in one transaction (completion_writer.dart:546-704); confirm the ticked item persists in Dashboard/Progress reads (completions_view) with NO network. If a marked item disappears or the UI spins on a network call, that is a network-gating regression (violates offline-first).
  - Reconnect drain only fires on a TRUE offline→online transition after a 1.5s debounce, then resets the Firestore channel and drains (sync_orchestrator.dart:526-555). The seeded first emission (previous==null) and duplicate "still online" emissions are intentionally ignored (sync_orchestrator.dart:534-535). On a fast flap back to offline within the debounce, the reset is skipped (sync_orchestrator.dart:545). Verify queued writes still push within ~1.5s of stable reconnect and that pending count drops to 0 (synced).
  - Status recompute can wedge or mislead: `_recomputeOutboxStatus` will NOT overwrite an in-flight `syncing` (sync_orchestrator.dart:976) and returns synced only if `_everPulledOnLaunch` (sync_orchestrator.dart:990). Watch for the badge stuck on "N pending"/"Syncing…" after the outbox actually empties, and confirm a stuck row (≥ degraded threshold attempts) surfaces as `degraded` "Sync paused — N queued" (sync_orchestrator.dart:981-987, backup_sync_section.dart:73-80) rather than silent loss.
  - Tombstone resurrection on inbound completions matches the natural key INCLUDING an EXACT eventTimestamp (drift_merge_store.dart:239-251 → findTombstonedEventByNaturalKey, completion_event_dao.dart:55). Unlike LWW kinds, completions have NO ±5s window here — a pulled completion whose timestamp differs by even seconds from the tombstone will NOT clear it and will INSERT OR IGNORE into a no-op, leaving the row dead. Test re-mark-after-expunge + remote round-trip for resurrection at second-level timestamp drift.
  - LWW ±5s tie-break can silently favor remote and overwrite a just-queued local edit: inside the window remoteIsNewer falls back to Firestore synced_at, and on any unresolved tie it returns `true` (prefer remote) (drift_merge_store.dart:132-145). Combined with the bookmark FK-guard that SKIPS a bookmark when its track hasn't synced yet (drift_merge_store.dart:412-418, fires `track_not_yet_synced` telemetry), watch for a newly-created-offline track's bookmark being dropped on first merge ordering, or a local track-state edit being clobbered by a near-simultaneous remote write.
- **Known risks:** Highest-risk defect points: (1) Completion tombstone-resurrection is timestamp-EXACT (drift_merge_store.dart:248 + completion_event_dao.dart:55) while LWW kinds get a ±5s window — a re-marked item pulled back with even seconds of timestamp drift silently stays tombstoned (data loss). (2) Reconnect drain depends on a clean offline→online edge with previous==false and a 1.5s debounce (sync_orchestrator.dart:534-545); a flapping or mis-seeded connectivity stream (connectivity_providers.dart:27 uses a probe that may report stale state) can cause queued writes to wait for the 60s periodic net (sync_orchestrator.dart:506) instead of pushing promptly. (3) Status badge truthfulness: `_recomputeOutboxStatus` won't overwrite `syncing` (sync_orchestrator.dart:976) and gates synced on `_everPulledOnLaunch` (990) — risk of a perpetual \"Syncing…\"/\"N pending\" that doesn't reflect an emptied outbox. (4) Bookmark-before-track FK ordering on merge (drift_merge_store.dart:412-418) can drop the bookmark of a track created offline on the first pull if ordering races; relies on a later listener re-delivery. (5) OutboxProcessor dead-letters after 10 attempts (outbox_processor.dart:108,232-243) — a persistently-denied push (e.g. undeployed Firestore rules for a new collection, per MEMORY) goes silently permanent; degraded state is the only UI signal. (6) All offline/sync UI strings are hard-coded English (offline_top_banner.dart:38; backup_sync_section.dart:34,64; sync_status_indicator.dart:26-63) — Hebrew-locale regression. (7) SyncStatusIndicator has no mount point, so the flow's \"indicator state transitions\" are only observable via Backup & Sync; an evaluator expecting an always-visible sync chip will mis-score. Product-rule guards to verify in passing: no track-type label leaks via merge back-compat shim (drift_merge_store.dart:330-332 maps is_active→state, must not surface a \"Personal/Standard\" label); chazara UI only when track.chazaraEnabled; tutor canMarkLiveCompletion=false must not be able to queue completions in a tutored session (outbox tutored-profile guard, outbox_processor.dart:209-215 blocks draining tutored-mirror data into the tutor namespace); persistent top profile switcher (app_shell tutor/child bars are tappable to showProfileSwitcherSheet) must remain reachable while offline; adults have no points so no points-ledger outbox rows for adult profiles; sentinel-date bulk-mark completions must still queue+push without leaking into streak/recent; back-dated enrolment generates past-dated catch-up tasks surfacing as overdue and those completions must round-trip; Hebrew terms binary + locale dates unaffected by sync.

### F5 Backup -> device restore (fresh device -> sign in -> restoreGuard -> DeviceRestoreScreen -> pull cloud -> populated Dashboard).

Wiring: SignInController.signInWithEmail/Google -> _navigateAfterSignIn (sign_in_controller.dart:344) sets cloud-born session, swaps the per-account DB file (invalidates userDatabaseProvider:386/401), best-effort pullOnLaunch (8s timeout, swallowed:429), counts profiles, then router.replaceAll([AppShellRoute]). AppShellRoute (app_router.dart:126-127) is guarded by [authGuard, restoreGuard, profileGuard] in that order. RestoreGuard.onNavigation (restore_guard.dart:40) sees a cloud account + empty local DB (no completions AND no profiles, :70) and router.replace(DeviceRestoreRoute) + resolver.next(false) (:83-84). DeviceRestoreRoute (/restore, app_router.dart:111) has NO guards. DeviceRestoreScreen.initState -> _startRestore -> service.restore() (device_restore_screen.dart:26-32). DeviceRestoreService.restore (device_restore_service.dart:132) writes 'in_progress' SharedPrefs marker, runs syncOrchestrator.pullOnLaunch (3-step UI: 0 pull / 1 curricula / 2 import), then derives active curricula from Drift trackDao.getActiveTracksForProfile(_profileId) and re-imports bundled content, writes 'complete' marker, fires restoreCompletedStream. On success _navigateAfterRestore (screen:79) markRestoreComplete + re-queries profileDao.getProfilesByAccount: 1 profile -> select first + AppShellRoute; >=2 -> ProfilePickerRoute; 0 -> AppShellRoute. DOUBLE-ACTION RISK: the _busy guard is per-card local state; the autoDispose pendingRedemptionsProvider removes the row only after invalidate(:99). A parent on a slow network double-tapping, or two parent devices acting on the same pending row, can race — fulfilRedemption has NO status guard (unlike declineRedemption :231), so a fulfil could overwrite a concurrent decline (LWW by updated_at, dao :384).
CONFIG-EMPTY EDGE CASES: PointConfigScreen shows pointConfigNoActiveTracksBody when no active tracks (:270-280); ChildRedemptionScreen shows redeemScreenNoRewards when no enabled milestones (:83-95); reward save with no track → rewardConfigNoActiveTracks snackbar (:218). Verify these empty states render rather than crashing, and that only isEnabled milestones appear in the child list (child_redemption_screen.dart:48-50).

### F9 — Bulk prior-progress / lifetime marking (sentinel-date credit). TWO distinct code paths, both stamping the sentinel DateTime.utc(2000,1,1):

PATH A — In-track bulk mark (source=bulkInTrack: suppresses streak+points, CREDITS siyumim+lifetime). Entry points: (1) CurriculumSettingsScreen after re-running the stage wizard auto-pushes BulkMarkScreen (curriculum_settings_screen.dart:174-178); (2) TrackDetailScreen "Mark as previously learned" tile -> _openBulkMark passes the track's scopeConstraints (track_detail_screen.dart:491-516,588-610). BulkMarkScreen phases: selection (HierarchySelectionPanel tri-state checkboxes, pre-ticks existing sentinel rows via isBulkPriorSentinel, search) -> confirmation (item count) -> processing -> done. On confirm, BulkPriorCompletionService.execute writes one completion per (item × ALL track stages, B6) with completedAt=kBulkPriorSentinelDate and creditsAchievement:true (bulk_prior_completion_service.dart:244-262); sets bookmark to first uncompleted; toast "...may unlock siyumim".

PATH B — Lifetime marking (source=lifetimeOnly: suppresses streak+points AND siyumim; lifetime-knowledge ONLY). Entry points: Settings header "Add Lifetime Learning" (settings_screen.dart:169), ParentSettingsScreen tile (parent_settings_screen.dart:227), LifetimeKnowledgeScreen FAB (lifetime_knowledge_screen.dart:170). LifetimeMarkingScreen -> per-curriculum cards -> LifetimeCurriculumMarkingScreen (HierarchySelectionPanel level-scope selections) -> Save -> recordCompletionsBatch (default source=lifetimeOnly) writes sentinel date, then invalidates lifetime/journey/progress providers; snackbar "N saved".

In both paths the sentinel date is below trackStartDate so streak math, pace, and recent-activity windows naturally exclude them; scheduler treats a lone stage-1 sentinel completion as a new-learning candidate (re-surfaces for actual study) rather than overdue.
- Screens: CurriculumSettingsScreen (entry A1: stage-wizard re-run auto-pushes BulkMark) → TrackDetailScreen (entry A2: 'Mark as previously learned' tile, passes scopeConstraints) → BulkMarkScreen — selection phase (tri-state hierarchy, pre-tick, search) → BulkMarkScreen — confirmation phase (item/record count + 'leave some unmarked' guard) → BulkMarkScreen — processing / done phase (result + tier toast) → SettingsScreen / ParentSettingsScreen / LifetimeKnowledgeScreen (entry B: 'Add Lifetime Learning') → LifetimeMarkingScreen (per-curriculum category cards with % progress) → LifetimeCurriculumMarkingScreen (level-scope select + Select-all + Clear + Save)
  - Tier-policy copy must match behaviour. BulkMark subtitle says counts toward siyumim+lifetime but NOT streak/points (l10n bulkMarkWizardSubtitle, app_en.arb:1694; rendered bulk_mark_screen.dart:487); Lifetime subtitle says NOT siyumim/streak/points (lifetimeMarkingSubtitle app_en.arb:1706; rendered lifetime_marking_screen.dart:86). Verify after marking: bulk -> siyum can unlock; lifetime -> siyum does NOT.

Non-live source forces completedAt=DateTime.utc(2000,1,1) (bulk_mark_completion_use_case.dart:83-85; learning_ledger_repository_impl.dart:146-150; bulk_prior_completion_service.dart:258). Tester must confirm streak counter and Recent Activity do NOT move after a bulk/lifetime mark (sentinel falls outside all recent windows — chart_data_service.dart:96-97).

Verify bulk-marked-but-not-relearned items still surface for actual study.

In Hebrew locale these stay English — verify against Hebrew-terms binary rule and locale.

Tester: un-tick a previously-marked seder/masechta, reopen, confirm it did not re-appear and Firestore tombstone propagated.

  - Provider-invalidation completeness on save: BulkMark invalidates dashboard%/lastCompletion/overviewStats/allDailyTasks (bulk_mark_screen.dart:398-403); Lifetime invalidates a larger set incl. siyumim-adjacent journey/progress (lifetime_marking_screen.dart:430-445). Verify Lifetime Knowledge %, dashboard, and (bulk only) Siyumim screen all refresh WITHOUT app restart — offline-first Drift reads, no network needed.
- **Known risks:** "HIGHEST RISK — tier leakage: the entire flow's correctness rests on the sentinel date keeping bulk/lifetime marks out of streak, points, and Recent Activity while still crediting siyumim (bulk only) and lifetime totals. Two separate sources (bulkInTrack vs lifetimeOnly) with different achievement gates mean a mis-set source = wrong siyum credit. Defects most likely at: (a) source defaulting — BulkMarkCompletionUseCase defaults bulkInTrack and recordCompletionsBatch defaults lifetimeOnly; any caller using the wrong entry leaks the wrong tier. (b) isBulkPriorSentinel uses moment-comparison because Firestore round-trip flips the isUtc flag (bulk_mark_screen.dart:117-126); a plain == regression silently breaks pre-tick AND every sentinel exclusion filter, re-polluting streak/recent. (c) B6 writes one row per ALL configured track stages, so siyum/lifetime counts can multiply unexpectedly if stage list is wrong (bulk_prior_completion_service.dart:240-262). LOCALIZATION RISK — BulkMarkScreen is heavily hardcoded English (title, guard snackbar, counts, confirmation/done copy) and Lifetime display names are stored as raw values for both He/En; both break the Hebrew-terms-binary + locale expectation. UI RISK — tri-state container checkbox math (_itemSelectionState) and the deferred-expunge path for un-ticked containers (resolvedItems==null) are subtle; mis-count or stale-record re-appearance on reopen is plausible. No tutor-gate is present on these screens — they are management surfaces, so confirm a tutor (canMarkLiveCompletion=false) reaches them via the child's parent-view as intended, and that the persistent top profile switcher remains visible throughout."

### F14 — Guard redirect chains for `/` (AppShellRoute). Guard order is fixed by route config order at app_router.dart:127 `guards: [authGuard, restoreGuard, profileGuard]`, then child-route guards `childModeGuard` and `pinGuard` apply only on the child/parent-mode routes (e.g. app_router.dart:214,229). auto_route runs guards sequentially; each `onNavigation` MUST end in exactly one `resolver.next(...)` or the NavigationResolver completer never completes = permanent hang. All five guards wrap their body in try/catch with an `if (!resolver.isResolved) resolver.next(...)` fail-safe (auth→SignIn, restore→OPEN/proceed, profile→OPEN/proceed, childMode→CLOSED/false, pin→CLOSED/false). Walk each path: (1) NOT-ONBOARDED — authGuard reads SharedPreferences `kOnboardingComplete`; if intro unseen → `router.replace(AppIntroRoute)` + `next(false)` (auth_guard.dart:51-56); intro seen + accounts on device → AccountPickerRoute, else SignInRoute (auth_guard.dart:60-73). (2) NEW-DEVICE — onboarded passes authGuard, restoreGuard checks `hasCloudAccount()` then empty-DB (no completions AND no profiles) → `router.replace(DeviceRestoreRoute)` (restore_guard.dart:57-87); local-only users skip (DNI-190). DeviceRestoreScreen on success calls `restoreGuard.markRestoreComplete()` (clears `_isNewDevice` cache) then routes by post-restore profile count: 1→AppShell, ≥2→ProfilePicker, 0→AppShell (device_restore_screen.dart:79-99). (3) NO-PROFILE — profileGuard: tutored session short-circuits to `next()` (profile_guard.dart:64-68); validates selectedProfileId against current account DB (handles stale id from account switch, profile_guard.dart:84-101); 0 profiles → `next()` to shell (NOT blocked) and AppShell jumps to Settings tab (profile_guard.dart:108-116 + app_shell.dart:134-140); 1 profile → auto-select + `next()`; 2+ none-selected → `router.replace(ProfilePickerRoute)` (profile_guard.dart:130-136). (4) CHILD-ROUTE-AS-ADULT — childModeGuard reads active profile `mode`; non-child (adult) → `next(false)` with NO redirect target, so navigation is silently aborted and user stays on current screen (child_mode_guard.dart:46-49). (5) PIN-GATED — pinGuard resolves PinScope (tutor scope wins if talmid active, else parent), `next(true)` if cached scope authenticated, else if no PIN set pushes PinFlowSetupRoute, else `promptForPin()` dialog; cancel/wrong → `next(false)` stays put (pin_guard.dart:90-127; router_provider.dart:56-123).
- Screens: /intro (AppIntroRoute) — not-onboarded, intro-unseen redirect target → /account-picker (AccountPickerRoute) — onboarded=false + accounts-on-device → /sign-in (SignInRoute) — onboarded=false + no accounts, AND authGuard fail-safe fallback → /restore (DeviceRestoreRoute) — new-device (cloud account + empty local DB) → /profile-picker (ProfilePickerRoute) — 2+ profiles none selected, or post-restore ≥2 → / → dashboard (AppShellRoute, initial tab) — clean resolve target; jumps to Settings tab if 0 own profiles → /settings (AppShell settings tab) — auto-target for profile-less / tutor-only adults → /parent-mode/* + /settings/lifetime/* (childModeGuard then pinGuard) — child-gated + PIN-gated routes → PinFlowSetupRoute / parent-PIN dialog / tutor-PIN dialog — pinGuard prompt surfaces
  - Onboarded path is the fast lane: authGuard returns `resolver.next()` immediately on `kOnboardingComplete==true` (auth_guard.dart:46-49) — verify a previously-onboarded user lands directly on Dashboard with NO flash of intro/sign-in. Fresh install must show intro slides (router.replace AppIntroRoute, auth_guard.dart:51-55), never a blank.
  - New-device redirect must show the restore screen's progress UI, not hang: DeviceRestoreScreen renders CircularProgressIndicator for `checking`/`restoring` states (device_restore_screen.dart:112-133); on `complete` it must auto-navigate via `_navigateAfterRestore` which calls `restoreGuard.markRestoreComplete()` THEN replaceAll (device_restore_screen.dart:82,92) — verify it does not bounce back to /restore (the `_isNewDevice` cache must flip to false, restore_guard.dart:36).
  - CHILD-ROUTE-AS-ADULT is the highest-risk no-redirect path: childModeGuard does `resolver.next(false)` with no `router.replace` for adult/null/missing-profile (child_mode_guard.dart:40-49) — verify the tap is silently aborted and the user STAYS on the current screen. A blank/white screen or an unresponsive-feeling dead tap here is the defect to catch.
  - ProfileGuard 0-profile path must NOT block — it calls `resolver.next()` to the shell (profile_guard.dart:108-116), then AppShell jumps to the Settings tab exactly once via post-frame `tabsRouter.setActiveIndex(3)` (app_shell.dart:134-140). Verify a tutor-only/profile-less adult lands on Settings (not stuck on empty Dashboard, not the picker).
  - Stale-selection guard: after an account switch, ProfileGuard re-validates `selectedProfileId` against the current account DB and re-resolves if it no longer exists (profile_guard.dart:84-101). Verify switching accounts surfaces the correct account's profile/picker, never the previous account's profile (per-account autoincrement IDs collide).
  - PIN gate must resolve, never strand: pinGuard pushes PinFlowSetupRoute when no PIN set, else opens the scope-correct dialog (parent vs tutor, router_provider.dart:61-106); cancel/wrong → `resolver.next(false)` keeps the user on the current screen (pin_guard.dart:113-118). Tutor-scoped routes must prompt the TUTOR PIN (keyed on tutorOwnProfileId), parent routes the parent PIN — verify the right dialog appears.
  - Persistent top profile switcher gap (memory: Daniel asked REPEATEDLY): `showProfileSwitcherSheet` is reachable ONLY from the tutor bar / child-view banner GestureDetectors in AppShell (app_shell.dart:329,410); on the plain adult/learner shell (no tutor session, no parent-mode elevation) the appBarBuilder collapses to just the offline banner and the Dashboard screen has no role-label header — verify whether the always-present tappable Learner/Adult/Tutor switcher is actually present in every context (likely MISSING on the default shell).
  - Fail-safe completion on every guard (no-lockout invariant): each guard's catch block does `if (!resolver.isResolved) resolver.next(...)` — auth→SignIn (auth_guard.dart:80-83), restore/profile→OPEN proceed (restore_guard.dart:94 / profile_guard.dart:52), childMode/pin→CLOSED false (child_mode_guard.dart:56 / pin_guard.dart:125). Verify forcing an error (e.g. locked DB) never leaves the resolver un-completed = permanent navigation hang.
- **Known risks:** "HIGHEST RISK — childModeGuard's adult-blocked path (child_mode_guard.dart:46-49) is the only guard in the chain that does `next(false)` with NO redirect target; an adult deep-linking/tapping a /parent-mode/* or /redeem route gets a silent no-op that can read as a dead/unresponsive tap or (if the destination already partially mounted) a blank — no error surface. SECOND — restoreGuard's session cache `_isNewDevice` (restore_guard.dart:32) is only cleared by `markRestoreComplete()`; if a navigation path reaches AppShell post-restore WITHOUT calling it, the guard re-fires `replace(DeviceRestoreRoute)` and loops the user back to restore (mitigated in device_restore_screen.dart:61,82 but fragile — any new exit path must call it). THIRD — multi-guard chain ordering: childModeGuard runs BEFORE pinGuard on parent-mode routes (app_router.dart:214,229); if childModeGuard fails-closed first, the PIN dialog never shows, so a parent on an ADULT profile can never reach parent-mode routes at all (parent mode is designed around a CHILD profile being active + PIN elevation, app_shell.dart:86-98) — verify this matches product intent and doesn't dead-end an adult. FOURTH — persistent-switcher requirement (memory flag, repeatedly requested) appears unmet on the default learner/adult shell: switcher entry exists only behind tutor/child banners (app_shell.dart:329,410), so 'switcher present in every context incl. parent portal' is likely violated. FIFTH — Hebrew/RTL + locale: switcher role label is binary `profileTypeChild`/`profileTypeAdult` (profile_switcher_sheet.dart:244-245) — verify Hebrew renders RTL with no clipping and adults show no points anywhere in these guard-redirect surfaces (adults-have-no-points rule). Product-rule cross-checks for these screens: no track-type label, chazara UI only when track.chazaraEnabled, tutor canMarkLiveCompletion=false (parent-view, live-mark barred) — none should leak into intro/sign-in/restore/picker surfaces."
